description:
Find and remove dead, stale and duplicated CODE, so the tree is what it claims to be.

RUN THIS LAST, DELIBERATELY. It carries a high number because a cleanup that runs before the work is finished deletes scaffolding that was about to be used, and then the next tasklist re-adds it. The roadmap should be substantially complete before this executes.

WHAT COUNTS AS DEAD. Unreferenced modules, functions and files; duplicated implementations of one behaviour; code behind flags that can no longer be set; scripts nothing runs; dependencies nothing imports; commented-out blocks kept 'just in case'. What does NOT count: code a test exercises, code an external consumer calls, and code that is deliberately unexercised and says so.

THE STANDARD OF PROOF, AND IT IS THE WHOLE TASKLIST. This portfolio has repeatedly found things that LOOKED dead and were not — a Prolog corpus reached by a path nobody found, `content_qa` declared callerless when it had a caller, `docs/studioos` cited by 93 files. Deletion is irreversible in effect even when git remembers, because nobody re-reads a deleted file. Every removal names the search that found nothing.

PAIRED WITH THE DOCS SWEEP, WHICH RUNS AFTER. Removing code changes what the docs should say, so the docs tasklist depends on this one. Do not fix docs here beyond what a removal strands.

userStories.title: An inventory, measured before anything is removed
userStories.notes: Inventory landed at docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md, linked from docs/README.md. GATE GREEN: `.chief/verify.sh --run docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md docs/README.md` → guard-doc-integrity OK (57 markdown files, 1399 relative links checked, 0 errors, all 3 status tables match their headers) and guard-doc-links "0 dead vs 0 on main" → "all selected gates green". Contents: Class A = 4 removal candidates, each with its search — EXCEPT_DIRS (docs/.structure-exceptions: 0 commits on any branch), IGNORE (docs/.linkignore: 0 commits), the docs/archive/ skip (0 commits, 0 grep hits outside scripts/), and the cross-repo `foreign` walk (0 of 65 tracked JSON files carry a repo/owner key, and it spawns `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` once per JSON file to compute a value that is wrong in a worktree and never compared). Class B = 1 duplicated implementation, measured not asserted: relative Markdown link resolution runs in both doc guards, 1371 of check-doc-links's 1371 md-link checks also done (more strictly, with anchors) by check-doc-integrity, its unique value being 8 bare docs/… citations in 3 non-Markdown files; recorded as a finding rather than a deletion because merging a ratchet into a wall changes the merge gate's failure semantics. Plus B-2, the 4th status mirror in CLAUDE.md that no guard checks. Class C = 5 survivors with the reason each survived: 8 registry rows with 0 in-repo citations (published vocabulary, signature immutable once published), the tasks/chief/completed/ skip (deliberately unexercised — hides 0 dead citations today, fires the day a doc moves), --json/--strict/--list (settable by hand, so not "flags that can no longer be set"), SKIP_DIR/SKIP_EXT, and the schema fixtures. Plus 9 searches that came back empty (0 orphan .md of 57, 0 orphan schemas, 0 unreferenced $defs of 10 with 80 $refs all resolving, 0 duplicated subschemas that were not already shared by $ref, 0 orphan entity types/enum tokens, 0 commented-out code blocks, no package.json at all, 0 dead branches in verify.sh, 0 unrun guard scripts).
acceptanceCriteria: Produce a checked-in inventory of candidates with, for each, the SEARCH that found it unreferenced — the command and its scope. A candidate list without its method is unreviewable, and this is the artifact a human approves before deletion.
Separate genuinely-dead from deliberately-unexercised. The second class exists here on purpose (refusal paths, guards, unreached tiers that say so) and deleting it removes a stated contract.
Include duplicated implementations as first-class findings, not just unused ones — two implementations of one behaviour is the failure mode that costs most later, because they drift.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: Removal, with the tree still green and the reason recorded
userStories.notes: Four reviewable commits, one candidate each, gate re-run after every one — and one of them is a RETRACTION. REMOVED (3 of 4 Class A candidates, 43 lines from scripts/check-doc-links.mjs, 168 -> 125, `git diff --numstat main` = 0/43): 68b860a EXCEPT_DIRS+IGNORE (A-1/A-2 — docs/.structure-exceptions and docs/.linkignore have 0 commits on any branch and 0 citations outside this record); a261ebb the cross-repo `foreign` walk (A-4 — 0 of 65 tracked JSON files carry a repo/owner key, no active tasklist plans one; removed 65 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` spawns per run that computed a value wrong in a worktree and never compared it; behaviour identical either side, --json = {total:0,distinct:0} before and after, wall clock 0.28/0.24/0.23s -> 0.23/0.09/0.08s). NOT REMOVED: A-3, the docs/archive/ skip — deleted in 2ee74d1 and REVERTED in c5b4bdf. Re-running its third search at commit time returned the hit the inventory reported as empty: tasks/chief/901-docs-tell-the-truth.json:48 mandates `docs/archive/` (US-3 AC-1, the paired docs sweep that runs next and depends on this tasklist). Scaffolding about to be used — exactly the failure the tasklist description names. Both commits kept unsquashed as the evidence. NO TEST DELETED, WEAKENED OR ADJUSTED: .chief/verify-test.sh byte-unchanged across all four commits, as is every spec/schema/registry/policy/scenario file. GATE GREEN AFTER EVERY STEP and at the end: `.chief/verify.sh --run docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md scripts/check-doc-links.mjs tasks/chief/900-dead-code-paydown.json` -> guard-doc-integrity OK (57 markdown files, 1410 relative links, 0 errors, all 3 status tables match their headers), guard-doc-links "0 dead vs 0 on main" (a ratchet: it runs the PRE-removal script in a temp worktree of main, so this is measured, not tautological), guard-categories OK 4 tasklists, guard-schemas OK 9 schemas/278 positions/80 $refs/3 fixtures, guard-registry OK 29 relation names -> "all selected gates green"; `bash .chief/verify-test.sh` -> 30 passed, 0 failed. SURVIVORS RECORDED in docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md: new section "The removal pass — three of four, and the one whose search was wrong" (per-commit table + the two reusable rules: re-run every search AT REMOVAL TIME, and ask "is it used, OR ABOUT TO BE"); every A-entry carries a Disposition line; A-3 reclassified into Class C, which now reads six entries; C-2 corrected — it and A-3 are the SAME verdict (both deliberately unexercised), not opposite ones; stale line refs fixed (C-2 76-79 -> 56-59, C-3 ratchet --json 136 -> 93).
acceptanceCriteria: Remove what US-1 established, in reviewable steps rather than one sweep. A single commit deleting hundreds of lines across unrelated subsystems cannot be reviewed and cannot be partially reverted.
The full gate passes after each step. A removal that needs a test deleted to stay green is a removal of something live — say so and stop rather than adjusting the test.
Anything NOT removed that looked dead is recorded with why it survived. That record is worth more than the deletions: it is what stops the next sweep re-litigating the same files.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: What the sweep could not decide
acceptanceCriteria: Report candidates the sweep could not resolve — reachable only through dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, or a consumer outside this repo — and leave them in place. An honest 'undecidable' list is a legitimate result.
State the limits of the method: what a static search over this tree cannot see. Cross-repo consumers are the obvious one, and this portfolio has already been bitten by exactly that.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.
